items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: I spent about two or three years living with an aunt that lived in Ranken, Pennsylvania, my mother's brother's wife in that family... that's when Aunt Jo -- her name was Josephine

ctx.x: when I was 3 years old. I used to sit up on the shoe shine -- they had a shoe shine man and I used to sit up there. I remember my father when I'd come in, he'd sit me up on the stand and go through the procedure of shining my patent leather shoes. But that's just about as much as I can remember. I remember going to the funeral and in those days they had the hearses with the horse and carriages and I cried but I was crying because I wanted to be in the hearse with my mother. I guess I was with somebody else at the…

But shortly after that I spent about two or three years living with an aunt that lived in Ranken, Pennsylvania, my mother's brother's wife in that family. And that's where I spent the early part of my childhood. I learned how to read and write and I guess I was quite a precocious kid because that's when Aunt Jo -- her name was Josephine, my uncle's name was Paul.
